data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek name Aikaterine, meaning 'pure, clear, shining'. In the New Testament, Catherine is the name of a martyr who refused to renounce her faith in Christ. The name Katy carries the meaning “Pure, Clear” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Katy usually hope their child will grow to embody pure, clear and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Katy belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Pure, Clear.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Katy total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.
data.cultural_impact: The name 'Katy' has been popular in Western culture throughout history. It shares a similar origin with the name 'Katherine', which appeared as a common given name during the Middle Ages, especially in Europe.
data.spiritual_significance: The name 'Katy' is deeply rooted in the Christian faith, as it comes from the name of St. Catherine of Alexandria. She is the patron saint of philosophers, mathematicians, and spinsters. Her legend involves many miracles and her unwavering commitment to her faith, inspiring those with the name Katy to follow a similar path of purity and dedication.
